title: Stopping a durable runner leaves its detached tool process groups running
body:
stopTree (stuck stop, wall clock, supervisor signal) and cancel signal only the runner's own process group. pi-durable's NodeExecutionEnv spawns every bash tool detached, so each tool leads its own group and survives the stop, orphaned to init/launchd. A hung tool keeps running forever, and because it can inherit the runner's lock fd it may keep the attempt's liveness lock held. Reproduced: with the l6n interrupt disabled, TestAStuckDurableWorkerInAHungToolIsSteeredThroughIt ends stopped as stuck and leaves 'bash -c …; sleep 3600' plus its sleep alive. The fix is probably to call interruptToolGroups (interrupt.go) on the runner before stopTree, and in cancel.go.
evidence: internal/exec/subprocess/supervisor.go stopTree; pi-durable dist/env/node.js spawn(..., { detached: true }); ps after the base's stuck stop shows the orphaned group with ppid 1
